items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: I remember that very well. I heard the first performance of that.

ctx.x: I understand that. I understand it personally very well, but you know, you may be right. I'm just questioning it because he wouldn't teach composition; he would teach piano but not composition.
Well apparently Koussevitsky, not long before Bartok died, got him to write "Concerto for Orchestra" for the Boston Symphony.
I remember that very well. I heard the first performance of that.
